releases.description:
## ⌨️ Changed

**The built-in hotkeys are offered now rather than imposed.** Fourteen commands used to arrive with keys already on them — a single-Alt layout tuned to one person's habits, down to a Russian-layout twin for every letter binding. Whether they are registered at all is a setting now, under a new "Hotkeys" heading.

**Nothing is pulled out from under a vault that already has them.** If the plugin was installed before this release, the setting comes on and every key keeps working exactly as it did. Only a fresh install starts bare — and bare is not the same as unusable: every command is in the command palette, and Obsidian's hotkey settings will bind any of them to anything you like. Your own assignments always beat the plugin's defaults, and that has not changed.

Commands are registered when the plugin loads, so switching this takes effect after the plugin is reloaded. The setting says as much, and a notice repeats it.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/mrrepac/obsidian-songwriter-player/compare/1.5.1...1.6.0

releases.description:
A small accessibility release.

## ♿ Fixed

**The controls have names now.** Every button carrying an icon and no text — the transport row, eject, open externally, the inline player's play button, the volume slider, the marker flag beside a playlist row — had nothing a screen reader could announce. They carry proper labels now, and the tooltips are unchanged.

Controls that do have visible text, like the playlist rows and the track name, are announced as buttons rather than as plain text, so it is clear they can be clicked. The playlist header reports whether it is open — the same thing its chevron says visually.

**A row could claim a marker it no longer had.** Removing a track's marker cleared the flag icon from its playlist row but left the description behind, so hovering the empty spot still said the track had one.

## 🔧 Under the hood

The project has tests now, run on every push and before a release is created. They bundle the source exactly as it ships and drive it against a stub Obsidian, so what is checked is the file you install. The first suite guards what survives a restart — the class of bug that lost per-track speed and key settings in 1.4.0 and was not caught until 1.4.1.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/mrrepac/obsidian-songwriter-player/compare/1.5.0...1.5.1

releases.description:
## ✨ New

**The keyboard's media keys reach the player.** Play/pause and next/previous track now work without switching to Obsidian first — hit the key while writing in another window and the beat stops. The track also appears in the system's now-playing card, the one Windows slides in with the volume overlay, titled with the track and the note or folder it was picked up from, and its scrubber seeks.

Previous and next are handed over only while there is a playlist to walk, so the system never offers a button that would do nothing. There is a toggle in the settings if another player should keep the media keys.

## 🔍 On the mobile half

This is desktop-only, and not by choice. A plugin can fill the media session in, but something has to carry it to the operating system, and inside Obsidian mobile that is the app's job rather than the page's — so no card appears on the lock screen or in the notification shade. Checked on a device rather than assumed. The plugin fills the session in there anyway, since it costs nothing and cannot misbehave, in case that ever changes; only the setting is hidden, so it stops promising what it cannot deliver.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/mrrepac/obsidian-songwriter-player/compare/1.4.1...1.5.0

releases.description:
A bug-fix release for 1.4.0.

## 🐞 Fixed

**Playback speed and transposition survive a restart.** They are meant to be remembered per track — a beat you are learning stays slow, a song stays in the key you sing it in — and they were being saved correctly, but thrown away again the next time Obsidian started. If you set a speed or a key in 1.4.0 and found it back at the recording the following day, this was why. Values are restored within the range the player can set (0.5–2×, ±12 semitones), and a track whose only setting is a speed or a key is no longer discarded as empty.

**"Open track's note" no longer loses its way.** Clicking an audio file in the file explorer used to drop the link back to the note the track was picked up from — even when it changed nothing about what was playing. The note now travels with the track as it loads, so `Alt+D` keeps working after a look at the file list, in manual mode, and after accepting an offered switch.

**The playlist stays where you left it.** Every track change rebuilt the whole list, which reset its scroll to the top — so on a folder of any size, ⏭ sent the view back to the first file while the track that was actually playing sat somewhere off screen. The list is now rebuilt only when the playlist itself changes; stepping through it moves the highlight and scrolls the playing track into view.

**Listened time is counted by the clock.** An hour of practice at 0.5× counted as half an hour, and "count a play after 5 seconds" waited for 10. Both now measure real seconds regardless of playback speed.

**Inline players resolve their file against the right note.** In a split, a background tab or a hover preview, an embedded track was looked up as if it were linked from whatever note happened to be in focus — which could find a same-named file in a different folder.

## 🔧 Under the hood

- The observer that catches embedded players sees every DOM change in the app, including each keystroke in the editor; its cleanup sweep now runs at most once per frame.
- `package.json` declared MIT while the project moved to AGPL-3.0 in 1.4.0, and its version had been left at 1.2.0. Both now match the rest of the repository.
- CI builds and type-checks every push and pull request, instead of finding out at release time.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/mrrepac/obsidian-songwriter-player/compare/1.4.0...1.4.1

releases.description:
## ⚠️ The licence changed: MIT → GNU AGPL-3.0

This release measures tempo and key with [essentia.js](https://github.com/MTG/essentia.js) (Music Technology Group, Universitat Pompeu Fabra), which is AGPL-3.0 — so the plugin as a whole now is too. Using it carries no obligations; distributing a modified build means keeping the source open under the same licence. `main.js` grows from 0.1 MB to 2.7 MB because the analysis library is compiled into it — Obsidian installs exactly three files, so it cannot ship alongside.

## ✨ New

**Tempo and key, measured.** A badge next to the track name shows `140 · F#m`. Measured once per file, in a worker — the analysis takes a few seconds and never blocks typing or playback — then remembered.

- **Two independent tempo estimators cross-check each other**, and the number comes from the one that proved more accurate on real tracks. Verified against tracks whose tempo was known: 160, 122 and 131 all came out exactly right, including one where a single estimator would have rounded to 162.
- **The preferred range folds the octave** — a beat heard at 160 or at 80 is a matter of feel, so the result lands in 80–159 by default (adjustable; the range is exactly one octave, so every tempo maps to a single value). `×2` and `÷2` in the badge menu override it per track.
- **Five key profiles vote**, from both the classical and the EDM-oriented families. When they split — which happens on the mode, not the tonic — the badge says so, offers both, and plays the tonic triad of either so it can be settled by ear. Your correction is final: analysis never overwrites it.

**Play slower or faster with the key intact.** The badge in the transport row shows the tempo it is actually playing at — 105 instead of 140 — rather than an abstract factor. `Alt+-` / `Alt+=` step by one bpm, `Alt+0` returns to the recording. Kept per track: a beat you are learning stays slow until you speed it up.

**Transpose without touching the tempo** (desktop). `Alt+PageUp` / `Alt+PageDown` move by a semitone, and the menu lists the target keys, so it reads "+2 — Abm" rather than "+2". The shifter is inserted between the player and the speakers only when a shift is actually asked for, so an untransposed track plays exactly as it did before.

**Save what you hear as a file.** Once the key fits, the badge menu writes a copy next to the original — `beat-tone+2bpm140.wav` — with the transposition and the speed baked in. It is an ordinary file: it plays with the marker, the A-B zone, the waveform and the playlist, drags into a note, and opens in a DAW.

## 🔍 On the sound

The shifter is granular with phase-aligned grains, tuned against measurements rather than by ear alone: grains are stitched with a crossfade (overlap-add would ripple the level once alignment moves a grain), resampled with a cubic interpolator, and the aligner prefers the smallest move among equally good ones. Against the first working version this cut spectral distortion by ~2.5 dB, raised level fidelity from 0.90 to 0.95, and halved the delay to ~36 ms. A 1024-sample grain measured better than 2048 and 4096 — a longer window holds sustained notes better but smears drums, which is the wrong trade for beats.

Pitch accuracy is within ~0.5 cents of the requested note, and the tempo does not move: checked on synthetic tones, on rendered files decoded back from disk, and on audio captured live from the player's own output.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/mrrepac/obsidian-songwriter-player/compare/1.3.0...1.4.0

releases.description:
## ✨ New

**Playlists.** A note holding several audio files lines them up as its playlist — and so does a folder: open any audio file and every audio file next to it queues up, sorted the way the file explorer sorts them (`№2` before `№10`), starting on the one you actually clicked.

- **The list lives under the player**, collapsible and remembering whether you left it open. Its heading names the source — the note or the folder — and counts the files.
- **Every row carries its history**: the play counter, and a ⚑ when the track has a marker, so a folder of demos tells you at a glance which ones you have been working on.
- **A click switches tracks without breaking the flow** — if something was playing, the new track keeps playing; a click on the current row is play/pause.
- **`⏮ ⏭` in the transport** walk the list and grey out at its ends, with `Alt+B` / `Alt+N` (and the Russian layout `Alt+И` / `Alt+Т`) doing the same from the keyboard.
- **The list outlives the track**: eject with ⏏ and it stays, so the next take is one click away.
- **Opening a note without audio no longer clears it** — the playlist belongs to the track you are working on, not to the page you happen to be reading, so lyrics and notes can be flipped through while the beats stay queued.

**Drag a track into a note.** Pull a playlist row (or the name of the loaded track) into the editor and an embed of that file lands at the cursor — rendered by this plugin as a waveform player. The link is generated by Obsidian itself, so it follows the vault's link format and path settings.

**Two new settings** under a *Playlist* heading:

- **Whole folder as a playlist** (on) — turn it off to load an opened audio file on its own.
- **Play the playlist through** (off) — when a track ends, the next one starts; the last one simply stops, and a track with an A-B zone keeps looping instead of moving on.

## 🐛 Fixes

- The playlist no longer stops at ~15 rows with empty space below it: the list claims the whole height the player leaves and scrolls inside itself only when it genuinely outgrows the panel, with the waveform and transport staying put.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/mrrepac/obsidian-songwriter-player/compare/1.2.1...1.3.0

## ⌨️ Changed

**The default hotkeys lost their `Ctrl`.** Transport keys are meant to be hit with one hand while the other one is on the guitar or the mouse, and `Ctrl+Alt+X` is not that. Every default is now a plain `Alt` chord:

| Command | Was | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Play from marker (or from start) | `Ctrl+Alt+X` | `Alt+X` |
| Stop | `Ctrl+Alt+C` | `Alt+C` |
| Set marker at current position | `Ctrl+Alt+A` | `Alt+Z` |
| Play/Pause | `Ctrl+Alt+P` | `Alt+P` |
| Open track's note | `Ctrl+Alt+S` | `Alt+D` |
| Seek back / forward | `Ctrl+Alt+,` / `Ctrl+Alt+.` | `Alt+,` / `Alt+.` |

"Set marker" moved from `A` to `Z` and "open track's note" from `S` to `D` on purpose: `Alt+A` and `Alt+S` are popular editor bindings, while `Z X C` now sit next to each other under the left hand.

Notes:

- **Your own bindings are untouched.** Anything you had rebound in Settings → Hotkeys stays as it is — new defaults only apply to commands you never touched. To pick up the new scheme on a command you had rebound, reset it there.
- **The Russian keyboard layout is still duplicated** for every binding (`Alt+Ч`, `Alt+С`, `Alt+Я`, `Alt+З`, `Alt+В`, `Alt+Б`, `Alt+Ю`).
- **macOS:** Option+letter produces a special character, so plain `Alt` defaults may not fire there — rebind the transport commands to a `Cmd`- or `Ctrl`-based chord in Settings → Hotkeys.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/mrrepac/obsidian-songwriter-player/compare/1.2.0...1.2.1

releases.description:
## ✨ New

**Waveform players inside your notes.** The plain embedded audio players (`![[demo.mp3]]`) are now replaced with a compact waveform wired to the very same player as the sidebar — no more bare grey control bar. Click the wave to play from anywhere, drag to select an A-B loop, double-click to drop your work marker — all in place, right in the note.

- **One player, everywhere.** The embed you're playing shows the live playhead and its button mirrors play/pause; the others stay as a static waveform (with their saved marker and loop) until you tap them. Only one track plays at a time, and the marker, loop zone, play counts and volume all stay in sync with the sidebar.
- **Reading view and Live Preview** — both are covered.
- **Light on resources.** A file's waveform is analyzed only once its player scrolls into view, the peak cache is shared with the sidebar (one decode per file), and idle waveforms park their redraw loop — so a note full of demos stays snappy.
- **New toggle "Waveform players in notes"** (Settings → Songwriter Player, on by default). Turn it off to get the plain player back plus the "open externally" button, exactly as before. Fully localized (EN/RU).

## 🐛 Fixes

- The waveform animation loop now suspends itself when nothing is moving, instead of redrawing at 60fps while idle.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/mrrepac/obsidian-songwriter-player/compare/1.1.0...1.2.0

releases.description:
## ✨ New

**Mobile floating button.** A round play button now floats over the note on mobile. Tap it to play from your work marker (or the start) without swiping over to the sidebar player — it sits in the top-right corner and keeps the editor focused, so the on-screen keyboard stays up.

- **Two tap modes** (Settings, mobile only):
  - **Always from marker** (default) — every tap (re)starts the track from the marker.
  - **Smart play/pause** — tap plays from the marker while paused, pauses while playing.
- Enable/disable toggle. Fully localized (EN/RU).

## 🐛 Fixes

- **Track-switching race** — rapidly switching tracks could briefly show the wrong track or apply another track's marker. Loads are now guarded by a token, so a superseded load can't touch the player.
- **Waveform decode cache** — a transient decode failure no longer sticks forever; the waveform retries on the next load instead of staying blank.
- **Playhead on a paused seek** — the cursor now moves when you seek while paused (previously only the time readout updated).
- Internal cleanup: removed dead code, merged duplicate pointer branches, tidied imports.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/mrrepac/obsidian-songwriter-player/compare/1.0.2...1.1.0
